subject: health
unitTitle: Navigating Health Systems, Coverage, and Confidentiality
title: Guided practice: what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist
focus: what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist
essentialQuestion: How does a person actually get care, and what does it cost them to try?
materials: course-supplied fictional coverage summaries and case files
keyPoints: Care costs reflect service price, setting, coverage, network, and assistance; community clinics, public programs, payment plans, and financial-assistance policies may reduce barriers.
Match the need to the appropriate service or administrative step, ask about access, cost, and privacy, and confirm what action or document comes next.

For what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Run three fictional cases through the system: choose the right level of care, estimate the cost path, prepare the questions, and identify the confidentiality rule that applies.
studentTask: Route two supplied fictional needs involving what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist. For each, choose the appropriate service or administrative step, list two access or privacy questions to ask, and write the next action the fictional person can complete without disclosing unrelated details.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Walkthroughs may be written, charted, narrated, or completed on a supplied decision frame with vocabulary pre-defined.
extensionChallenge: Apply what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.

Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of what care costs without coverage, and where low-cost options exist in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.
